title: Direct sums of uniformly bounded families
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=\underline E$ or $\underline{\Qlb}$ be the condensed coefficient ring of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and let $p:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For $T=X,Y$, use the pulled-back coefficient ring $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], its category of module sheaves [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and its unbounded derived category $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], in the fixed site and indexing universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $\operatorname{IndCons}(T,\Lambda)$ for the module sheaves that are small filtered colimits, in $\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$, of constructible module sheaves [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and $D_{\mathrm{ic}}(T,\Lambda)$ for the full subcategory whose cohomology sheaves belong to $\operatorname{IndCons}(T,\Lambda)$ in every degree. Let $F=Rp_*$ be the total right derived functor of module pushforward [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

Let $I$ be any small set, $a,b\in\mathbf Z$, and $(M_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$ a family in $D_{\mathrm{ic}}(X,\Lambda)$ satisfying $H^r(M_\alpha)=0$ whenever $r<a$ or $r>b$. For the ambient derived coproducts, the canonical comparison
$$
\eta_M:\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}F(M_\alpha)\longrightarrow F\Bigl(\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}M_\alpha\Bigr),
\qquad \eta_M\circ\iota_\alpha=F(\iota_\alpha),
$$
is an isomorphism in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$.

proof.text: Set $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$. On the small site skeletons and in the universes fixed in the statement, these are Grothendieck abelian categories and have K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; this theorem applies to the commutative ring sheaf $\Lambda_T$, not to a discrete constant replacement. They also have enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives], so the bounded-below comparisons used in step 4 have this hypothesis. Module pushforward is additive and left exact by [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], and $F$ is its unbounded derived functor by [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Thus [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] makes $F$ additive, shift-compatible and triangulated. For every family $N$, define $\eta_N$ by the coproduct equation $\eta_N\iota_\alpha=F(\iota_\alpha)$. The universal property gives existence, uniqueness and naturality in componentwise maps of families; this is the comparison under consideration.

source.place: Proof, comparison-map paragraph; K-injective framework: Stacks Tags 07A5 and 079P; triangulated derived functor: cited project theorem

proof.text:
We record the elementary cone calculation used below. By [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts], coproducts in each $D(\mathcal A_T)$ are represented by termwise sums of arbitrary representative complexes. For chain maps $u_\alpha:A_\alpha\to B_\alpha$, the cone formula of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives a canonical isomorphism
$\bigoplus_\alpha C(u_\alpha)\cong C(\bigoplus_\alpha u_\alpha)$: in degree $r$, both sides are $(\bigoplus_\alpha B_\alpha^r)\oplus(\bigoplus_\alpha A_\alpha^{r+1})$, and their differential matrices are $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\oplus d_B&\oplus u\\0&-\oplus d_A\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. This identification respects the inclusions, projections and the signed boundary. Representing each distinguished triangle by a cone triangle and summing its isomorphism proves that any small sum of distinguished triangles is distinguished. Also $\bigoplus N_\alpha[s]\cong(\bigoplus N_\alpha)[s]$ by the degreewise shift formula. Finally [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums](1) supplies the canonical, coprojection-compatible identifications $H^r(\bigoplus N_\alpha)\cong\bigoplus H^r(N_\alpha)$ on $X$ and $Y$, as well as closure of $D_{\mathrm{ic}}$ under these sums. No assertion that an arbitrary triangulated category has exact infinite sums is used.

source.place: Proof, base-case cohomology and induction-step sum of triangles; Stacks Tag 07D9 (injectives-lemma-derived-products) and cone definition in Tag 05RU

proof.text: The direct-sum input on sheaves is [det-proper-heart-continuity-direct-image], applied to $p$ and $A=\Lambda_X$, with target scalars restricted along $\Lambda_Y\to p_*\Lambda_X$ as in the module pushforward. Its hypotheses hold: proper means finite type and separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]; finite type includes quasi-compactness [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated implies quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Consequently, for every family of module sheaves $B_\alpha$ and $q\geq0$, the canonical map $\bigoplus R^qp_*B_\alpha\to R^qp_*(\bigoplus B_\alpha)$ is an isomorphism. This uses exactly the continuity assertion underlying the direct-sum clause of the blueprint's proper-heart-bound lemma; it needs no uniform bound on fibre dimensions. The unit's invocation of the proper-heart-bound lemma cannot supply a uniform integer d from properness alone: the disjoint union of the proper maps $\mathbf P^m_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, for $m\geq0$, is a proper morphism to the disjoint union of these points, since properness is local on the target, but its fibre dimensions are unbounded. This is the missing hypothesis in that invocation; the existing continuity statement supplies just its direct-sum input while preserving the unit's shifted-heart and truncation induction.

source.place: Proof, base-case use of proper-heart-bound; its direct-sum input is the current continuity node in sec-proetale-coefficients/sk-cor-pe-bounded-continuity/sk-lem-proper-heart-continuity-direct-image.md; proper/qcqs definitions: Stacks Tags 01W1, 01T0, 01QO, 01KK

proof.text:
We prove the assertion for all intervals by induction on $b-a\geq0$, after disposing of empty intervals. If $a>b$, each $M_\alpha$ has zero cohomology in every degree, so $0\to M_\alpha$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]. The comparison is then the isomorphism $0\to F(0)=0$, including when $I$ is empty. Suppose $a=b$. By [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single], $M_\alpha\cong B_\alpha[-a]$, with $B_\alpha\cong H^a(M_\alpha)\in\operatorname{IndCons}(X,\Lambda)$. Transport the family and its coprojections through these isomorphisms. The shift comparisons from step 1 and the sum/shift and sum/cohomology identifications of step 2 identify $H^n(\eta_M)$ with
$$
\bigoplus_\alpha R^{n-a}p_*B_\alpha\longrightarrow R^{n-a}p_*\Bigl(\bigoplus_\alpha B_\alpha\Bigr).
$$
Here $H^q(F(B[0]))=R^qp_*B$ naturally for $q\geq0$ by [lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification] and the bounded-below/unbounded compatibility [src-right-derived-functor-plus-compatibility]. For $q<0$ both sides vanish, since the same identification computes $F(B[0])$ by an injective resolution starting in degree zero. The displayed map is the canonical one: on the $\alpha$th summand it is $R^{n-a}p_*(\iota_\alpha)$, by naturality of these identifications and the defining equation of $\eta$. For $n-a\geq0$ it is an isomorphism by step 3, and for $n-a<0$ it is $0\to0$. Hence $\eta_M$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]. The index is $n-a$, since $H^n(K[-a])=H^{n-a}(K)$.

source.place: Proof, base case a=b, with corrected shift sign; Stacks Tags 08J5, 015A, 05TH, 05TI and 05RT

proof.text: Assume $a<b$, and assume the assertion for every family supported in any interval of smaller nonnegative length. Put $L_\alpha=\tau_{\leq b-1}M_\alpha$ and $T_\alpha=H^b(M_\alpha)[-b]$. The canonical truncations of [def-kun-truncations] show that $L_\alpha$ has cohomology in $[a,b-1]$ and $T_\alpha$ in $[b,b]$. They belong to $D_{\mathrm{ic}}(X,\Lambda)$: truncation stability is [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums](2), while $T_\alpha$ has just the ind-constructible sheaf $H^b(M_\alpha)$ as its nonzero cohomology. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] and $\tau_{\leq b}M_\alpha\xrightarrow{\sim}M_\alpha$ (its cohomology map is the identity in the retained degrees and all other groups are zero, so use [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]), there is a canonical distinguished triangle $L_\alpha\to M_\alpha\to T_\alpha\to L_\alpha[1]$. The induction hypothesis makes $\eta_L$ invertible; the already proved length-zero case makes $\eta_T$ invertible.

source.place: Proof, induction-step truncation triangles; Stacks Tag 08J5 (derived-remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), with index b-1

proof.text: Sum the distinguished triangles $F(L_\alpha)\to F(M_\alpha)\to F(T_\alpha)\to F(L_\alpha)[1]$ to form the upper row, and apply $F$ to the summed triangles $\bigoplus L_\alpha\to\bigoplus M_\alpha\to\bigoplus T_\alpha\to(\bigoplus L_\alpha)[1]$ to form the lower row. Both rows are distinguished by the cone calculation of step 2 and [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. The maps $(\eta_L,\eta_M,\eta_T)$ form a morphism of these triangles. Indeed the square for either of the first two arrows, after precomposing with the $\alpha$th coprojection, is just $F$ applied to the defining coprojection square of the summed source triangle. For the boundary square the same calculation uses the coprojection $L_\alpha[1]\to(\bigoplus L_\alpha)[1]$; naturality of the shift isomorphism of $F$ identifies its composite with $\eta_L[1]$ with the shifted $F(\iota_\alpha)$. Thus the last square commutes with precisely the required shifted first component. Since the first and third vertical components are isomorphisms by step 5, [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes the middle component $\eta_M$ an isomorphism. This completes the induction and proves the claimed comparison for every small family.

Expanded the bounded-length induction, including empty intervals and empty families. Reused existing ringed-site, derived-coproduct, truncation, continuity and triangle-isomorphism interfaces; created no nodes. Replaced a missing ambient parent citation by its actual detail node, corrected n+a to n-a, and used the existing qcqs continuity input instead of assuming an unavailable global fibre-dimension bound. split_report.blueprint: Steps 1-2 realize the comparison paragraph and the sum/cohomology and sum/triangle facts of the base and induction paragraphs. Steps 5-6 realize the full truncation-triangle induction paragraph, including the last boundary square. The unit first paragraph is preserved: induction on a common interval via the shifted heart and truncation triangles.
